sources.articleTitle: INS Betwa set for major propulsion upgrade under Rs 498 crore deal
Defence Ministry inks ₹498 crore INS Betwa refit contract

headline: Indian Ministry Of Defence Finalizes INS Betwa Propulsion Upgrade
seoTitle: INS Betwa Propulsion Refit Contract Signed
metaDescription: The Indian Defence Ministry has signed a 498 crore rupee contract to modernize the propulsion system of the Brahmaputra-class frigate, INS Betwa.
aiSummaryBullets: The Indian Defence Ministry has awarded a 498 crore rupee contract for the refit of the frigate INS Betwa.
The project involves replacing the vessel's current steam-based propulsion with a diesel engine-based system.
INS Betwa belongs to the Brahmaputra class of frigates currently operated by the Indian Navy.
aiContextParagraph: The Indian Ministry of Defence recently formalized a contract valued at 498 crore rupees focused on the technical modernization of the INS Betwa. This naval vessel, which is classified as a Brahmaputra-class frigate, is slated to undergo a significant mechanical overhaul. According to official ministry statements, the primary objective of this agreement is to facilitate a complete transition of the ship's internal propulsion infrastructure. The current steam-based propulsion system will be removed and replaced with a modern diesel engine-based configuration. This upgrade is part of ongoing efforts to maintain and improve the operational capabilities of the existing naval fleet. While the project is a major technical undertaking for the vessel, it represents a standard procedure in naval maintenance and fleet management to ensure continued serviceability of Brahmaputra-class ships within the maritime defence framework of the region.
